notes: Reddit could not be read for this snapshot, so English-language sentiment comes mainly from Hacker News, which skews toward developers and benchmark skeptics.

linux.do pages could not be fetched directly. Each linux.do sample is one topic title found through site search, counted as one opinion; titles are short and often sarcastic, so their stance is a judgment call, and their dates are estimated from topic IDs.

Hacker News threads were read through the Algolia API and very large launch threads only partly. Treat positive/negative shares as accurate to roughly ±10 percentage points, and the sample size as distinct opinions actually read after approximate de-duplication.
Aspect scores range from -1 to 1 and reflect the themes in the sampled opinions; an empty value means no evidence, not a neutral view.
English- and Chinese-language communities sometimes disagree, for example on GPT-6 Astra, Kimi K3.1 Pro and GLM-5.3.
Reports of quality drops are user perceptions and are not verified. Where a drift tracker exists (LiveNerf for Claude Opus 5.5), it showed no measurable change through 2026-10-25.

Quotes are shown only when they are civil and on topic. Opinions that contain insults or allege misconduct still count toward the shares but are not quoted; the summaries describe such claims neutrally and attribute them.
Some comments rate several models at once (for example a benchmark table posted in a thread); these count as one opinion per model.
OpenRouter usage reflects API traffic, much of it cheap or free; it does not capture first-party subscription use such as Claude Code, Codex or the Gemini app.
